nodes.label: Two independent CI lanes (platform vs arena)
nodes.rationale: Gateway/model-service promotion and the arena share no code, dependency set, image content or host; a single changes: anchor caused a stylesheet edit to build the torch model-service image and an adapter.py edit to rebuild arena images unrelated to it.

nodes.label: Git-LFS pointer file exclude pattern
nodes.rationale: Model artifacts (tokenizer.json, *.onnx, *.bin, *.model) are Git LFS pointers; a hook editing one triggers the lfs diff driver to fetch and expand the real multi-MB artifact, which once truncated a CI job log at 4 MiB rendering one tokenizer.json diff.

nodes.label: gitleaks hook removal rationale
nodes.rationale: gitleaks was removed entirely rather than skipped: pre-commit provisions every declared repo's environment before deciding what to skip, so merely listing it forced a git fetch to github.com the runner cannot always reach; its actual coverage (staged-changes-only) was already a no-op in CI, which never has anything staged.

nodes.label: repo: local hooks pinned to uv.lock
nodes.rationale: ruff, black and pre-commit-hooks run as repo: local against versions already pinned in uv.lock rather than GitHub-hosted repos, so no fetch to github.com is needed since uv sync already put the binary on PATH.
nodes.norm_label: repo: local hooks pinned to uv.lock

nodes.label: NiFi ingestion routing (model-agnostic)
nodes.rationale: NiFi derives team_id only from the incoming path and sends file bytes plus that trusted value to the gateway; uploaded metadata cannot choose a team, API URL, or model.

nodes.label: Pipeline budget guidance
nodes.rationale: The pipeline avoids GitLab shared-runner minutes; keep GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE, the vps-ci default tag, the consolidated fast_checks job, change-based package rules, and the duplicate-pipeline workflow guard unless an intentional capacity review approves a change.

nodes.label: BuildKit IPv6 DNS pull retry rationale
nodes.rationale: The runner host has IPv6 while its build containers do not; when DNS returns a AAAA record first, BuildKit dials it and the Docker Hub pull dies instantly with network unreachable. It is a coin flip per lookup, so one retry is configured (concurrent=1 makes a second retry too costly).
nodes.norm_label: buildkit ipv6 dns pull retry rationale

nodes.label: OCR weights baked into image for QA rationale
nodes.rationale: qa_release_gate runs the downstream contract gate against published images, and GitLab services: cannot mount volumes, so the OCR fallback must be baked into the image for QA to reach it; production still prefers host-mounted artifacts verified by deploy-gateway.sh.
nodes.norm_label: ocr weights baked into image for qa rationale

nodes.label: mode=min export cache avoids disk exhaustion
nodes.rationale: This build installs torch and bytecode-compiles ~9,800 files; exporting every intermediate layer with mode=max meant materialising all of it in BuildKit's local content store before pushing, which ran the runner out of disk. mode=min caches only the final layers, trading full-layer caching for disk safety.
nodes.norm_label: mode=min export cache avoids disk exhaustion

nodes.label: Arena MLflow VPS separate host/variable-prefix rationale
nodes.rationale: The arena runs on a different host (leaderboard.mlflow.me) from the gateway's VPS. Every variable is MLFLOW_VPS_*-prefixed so it can never collide with the gateway's VPS_*/SSH_* CI/CD variables if a NiFi-VPS arena deployment is added later; allow_failure: true throughout so an arena failure never stops the gateway's own pipeline.
nodes.norm_label: arena mlflow vps separate host/variable-prefix rationale

nodes.label: Candidate identity crossing the project boundary
nodes.rationale: trigger:inputs cannot carry the candidate identity because GitLab does not expand CI/CD variables in input values downstream. trigger:variables cannot either: qa-automation's Pipeline variables setting is no_one_allowed, so a trigger job carrying variables: makes GitLab refuse to create the downstream pipeline entirely. The candidate identity is therefore resolved downstream by qa-automation's verify_candidate_contract.py, which queries this project's API for the pipeline whose bridge job points at the downstream pipeline's own CI_PIPELINE_ID.
nodes.norm_label: candidate identity crossing the project boundary

nodes.label: mirror-strategy trigger job holds no runner slot
nodes.rationale: Both qa_release_gate and qa_arena_evaluation use a native trigger with strategy: mirror rather than a script that polls the downstream API, because a mirrored trigger job holds no runner slot while it waits -- the VPS runners are configured concurrent = 1, so a blocking poller would occupy the only slot and deadlock against the pipeline it is waiting for.
nodes.norm_label: mirror-strategy trigger job holds no runner slot

nodes.label: Digest-to-commit-SHA registry tag aliasing
nodes.rationale: publish_gateway and publish_model_service only run on merge requests, so every registry tag is named after an MR head SHA and no tag for a default-branch commit ever existed, causing every arena evaluation to 404. load_production_candidate re-PUTs the same manifest under the main commit SHA (a manifest copy, not a rebuild) so the image a main SHA resolves to is byte-identical to the tested candidate.

nodes.label: squash/merge commit SHA mismatch resolution
nodes.rationale: CI_COMMIT_SHA on main is not guaranteed to be the commit the MR pipeline tested; squash-on-merge mints a new commit. load_production_candidate resolves the merged MR for this commit and uses the pre-merge source SHA that record_production_candidate actually recorded the package under, then republishes the manifest under the main commit SHA too since downstream QA finds the upstream pipeline via a default-branch SHA.

nodes.label: unset PROD_LOGS_S3 credentials disable audit upload
nodes.rationale: Leaving PROD_LOGS_S3_ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY unset means the per-request audit object is not written at all -- _upload_audit logs audit_upload_disabled and returns. deploy/compose.yml already defaulted these to empty; only this demo compose file demanded them, so running the demo previously meant holding the production logs bucket's credentials.

nodes.label: Platform Shared Regex Engine
nodes.rationale: Structured PII (identifiers, VAT numbers, postcodes, house numbers, emails, URLs, dates, phones) comes from the platform's shared regex engine, the same one Octo runs. Berts previously carried its own Belgian-only regex table until it was found printing a French national number in the clear.

nodes.label: AGE/DATE/PHONE_NUMBER Merge Policy
nodes.rationale: Neither the model nor regex owns AGE, DATE, or PHONE_NUMBER: both reach the merge and the span covering more of the value wins, with an exact tie going to the model. Berts used to drop every regex span carrying one of those three outright, leaving a value the checkpoint tagged only part of uncovered -- the Dutch model read '- 04-2025:' as '-2025' and the letter went out reading '- 04' in the clear beside the masked year.

nodes.label: MODEL_ID_SHAPE_GATE

Matters most for AGE, where the regex layer cannot cover for the model at all -- a prediction over a word instead of a number has no number under it for any pattern to find, and without the gate it is released redrawn as letters.

nodes.label: BERTS_LANGUAGE_ROUTING
nodes.rationale: Setting it to off sends every document to the Dutch checkpoint, restoring the single-model behaviour that predates the other two. It is the rollback for a bad checkpoint: one restart, no release.

nodes.label: CPU-only int8 ONNX Runtime
nodes.rationale: The only supported runtime format is CPU onnx. All three immutable artifacts are committed and tracked with Git LFS; a deployment stages all three together, because a missing one is not noticed at startup but at the first document in that language.

nodes.label: CHECKPOINTS config (teams/berts/runtime.py)
nodes.rationale: Documents what teams/berts/runtime.py:CHECKPOINTS pins. The name and revision have no environment override on purpose: with three artifacts a single MODEL_NAME could only rename all of them at once, and the point of naming one per language is that it matches the file that answered. Only the path and the approved digest are overridable, which is what a production mount of staged artifacts needs.

nodes.label: qa-pii-v1 label schema
nodes.rationale: Every checkpoint emits the same six labels -- ADDRESS, AGE, DATE, NAME, ORGANIZATION, PHONE -- with the same label2id, so label mapping to qa-pii-v1 and the merge policy are identical whichever checkpoint answered.

nodes.label: Idle Unloading of Checkpoints
nodes.rationale: Each checkpoint is loaded lazily, on the first document in its language, and all loaded checkpoints are dropped together by idle unloading. A deployment that only ever sees Dutch never pays memory for the other two; a mixed-language batch holds all three.

nodes.label: X-Model-Name / X-Model-Version Provenance
nodes.rationale: The returned provenance names the checkpoint that actually answered, so X-Model-Name and X-Model-Version differ between a Dutch and a French document from the same deployment. Deliberate: one name covering three artifacts would make the response provenance unable to say which weights produced the masked bytes.

nodes.label: Berts Validated Regex Layer
nodes.rationale: Checksum-validates Belgian INSZ, RIZIV, and VAT identifiers; detects email and URLs; rejects dosage, blood-pressure, and clinical-measurement hard negatives.

nodes.label: AGE/DATE/PHONE Merge Policy (model card)
nodes.rationale: AGE, DATE, and PHONE are owned by neither source: model and regex spans both reach the merge and the wider one is kept, so a value the checkpoint tags only part of is still covered whole.

nodes.label: French Checkpoint Over-masking
nodes.rationale: The French checkpoint over-masks: it emits occasional spurious spans on function words (de as AGE, à/la as ORGANIZATION) and over-spans organization names into the following sentence boundary. This is the safe direction -- more masked, not less -- and is checkpoint behaviour, not routing: no stopword filter is applied, because dropping model spans by surface form is exactly the kind of silent under-masking this service must not introduce.

nodes.label: Synthify Regex Supplement Merge Policy
nodes.rationale: runtime.py merges deterministic detections from regex_detectors.py into the model's own spans before returning them. It covers URL (model scores 0.078), plus checksum-validated INSZ (mod-97) and CREDITCARDNUMBER (Luhn) and structural RVIZ. On overlap the wider span wins, so the merge never shrinks masked coverage; merged spans carry source regex rather than model. Reported validation scores are model-only and exclude this supplement. Set REGEX_DETECTORS=off to get model-only spans.

nodes.rationale: Physician registration identifier format is country-specific (GMC number UK, RPPS France, RIZIV/INAMI number Belgium); each has a distinct numeric pattern the masker must match.

nodes.label: Sending Physician Name field
nodes.rationale: The sending physician can differ from the responsible physician (seen explicitly in the urology test fixture, where VERANTWOORDELIJKE and VERZONDEN DOOR name different doctors), so this must be treated as a distinct entity class from responsible_physician_name_field rather than assumed identical.

nodes.label: Urology Specialty
nodes.rationale: This fixture uses a different generation batch (dated 2024 vs. 2026) and punctuated ID formats (INSZ with dots, RIZIV with dashes) unlike the other nl-BE letters' unpunctuated digit strings, suggesting it probes the masker's tolerance for alternate identifier punctuation.
